chunk_findings.detail: `append_many` holds `self._lock` (`threading.Lock`, not reentrant) and then calls `append`, which acquires the same lock. Any call such as `append_many([("k", "s", {})])` deadlocks on the first item and never returns, so the batched append the port requires cannot complete.

chunk_findings.detail: The test never replays the EventLog records through the fake or compares the two stores. Given five `task.added` events with `data={"marker": i}` written by `EventLog`, `LocalLogStore.read_from(0)` can drop every marker (or rewrite lamports) and still pass, because only subjects are checked; `FakeLogStore` is then filled by a second `append` loop, so a fake that ignores `data` or assigns a different order key also passes. The docstring's claim that one real log replayed through both agrees is therefore false.

chunk_findings.detail: `_write` only shallow-copies the payload (`data = dict(data or {})`) and stores that dict on the frozen `_Event`. Given `payload = {"marker": {"n": 1}}`, `append("task.added", "s", payload)` then `payload["marker"]["n"] = 2`, `read_from(0)` returns `n == 2`. A jsonl log snapshots the bytes at append, so the recorded event must stay `1`; the fake rewrites history whenever the caller mutates a nested value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/log_store.py:90

chunk_findings.detail: `_events`, `read_from`, `snapshot`, and `shards` never take `_lock`, while `append` / `compact` mutate `_shards` under it. Interleaving: thread A is inside `_events` after `sorted(self._shards)` has yielded `"worker.jsonl"`; thread B runs `compact()`, which `del`s that shard before A indexes `self._shards[shard]`. A raises `KeyError`. The same race on `read_from` can also return a gap (an event with lamport L missing while L+1 from a later shard is present), so the ordered prefix the lock is supposed to protect is not actually observed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/log_store.py:98

chunk_findings.detail: `LogStore.append` treats `agent` as the shard name, but `LocalLogStore.append` drops that argument and always calls `EventLog.append(kind, subject, data)` on the instance built with `agent_id`. Given a store constructed with `agent_id="alice"` and `append("note", "s", {}, agent="bob")`, the event is written on alice's shard, not bob's, so two agents' appends are not isolated and a later `shards()` / `read_from` replay does not match the port (or a fake that honors `agent`).

chunk_findings.detail: `clip` repairs redaction marks and then word-breaks, so the word break can reopen a mark. `clip("see [REDACTED:my secret] end", limit=27, keep=24, boundary="word")` takes the first 24 characters, `"see [REDACTED:my secret]"`, which `whole_marks` keeps, then `rsplit(" ", 1)[0]` returns `"see [REDACTED:my"`. That ends inside the mark and drops the closing `]`, contradicting the contract on lines 81-82. Any later `rstrip` does not put the `]` back.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/textcut.py:97

chunk_findings.detail: `_after_mark` only sees a finished `\[REDACTED:[^\]]*\]`, so a tail or window can start inside an unclosed mark. `clip("hello [REDACTED:secret", limit=21, side="tail", keep=10)` yields `marker + "ED:secret"`. `window("[REDACTED:supersecret", 5, 20)` yields a leading marker plus `"CTED:supersecret"`. Neither call moves to a mark boundary, so the redacted payload is emitted as ordinary text.
